plain.text: Some men came from Judea to Antioch teaching that unless Gentile believers were circumcised according to Moses' law, they could not be saved. Paul and Barnabas strongly disagreed. So the church sent them with others to Jerusalem to see the apostles and elders about this question. Along the way they told how the Gentiles had been converted, which made all the believers very glad.

Some believers who belonged to the Pharisees said Gentiles must be circumcised and keep the law of Moses. The apostles and elders met to consider this. After much discussion, Peter said God had chosen him to bring the good news to the Gentiles. God had given them the Holy Spirit, just as he did to us, and made no distinction, purifying their hearts by faith. "Why are you putting a heavy load on them that neither we nor our ancestors could carry? We believe it is through the grace of our Lord Jesus that we are saved, just as they are." The assembly listened as Barnabas and Paul told about the signs God had done among the Gentiles. Then James said that Scripture agreed: God was taking from the Gentiles a people for his name. He judged they should not make it difficult for Gentiles turning to God, but write telling them to avoid food polluted by idols, sexual immorality, meat of strangled animals, and blood.

The apostles, elders and the whole church chose Judas (called Barsabbas) and Silas to go with Paul and Barnabas to Antioch with a letter. It said they had heard that some had troubled the Gentile believers without authorisation. "It seemed good to the Holy Spirit and to us not to burden you with anything beyond these requirements," and listed the four things to avoid. "You will do well to avoid these things."

At Antioch, the church gathered and read the letter, and the people were glad for its encouraging message. Judas and Silas, who were prophets, said much to encourage and strengthen the believers. Paul and Barnabas stayed in Antioch, teaching and preaching the word of the Lord with many others. (Verse 34 is not in the earliest manuscripts.)

Some time later, Paul suggested visiting all the towns where they had preached. Barnabas wanted to take John Mark, but Paul did not, because Mark had deserted them earlier. They had such a sharp disagreement that they parted company. Barnabas took Mark and sailed to Cyprus, but Paul chose Silas and went through Syria and Cilicia, strengthening the churches.

summary.bigIdea: The church meets in Jerusalem and agrees that Gentiles are saved by grace, without having to keep the whole law of Moses.
points: A big question: must Gentile believers be circumcised and keep Moses' law?
Peter: "It is through the grace of our Lord Jesus that we are saved, just as they are."
The council's letter brings joy; later Paul and Barnabas part ways over Mark.
summary.reflection: The church listened, discussed and sought the Spirit's guidance together. How do you handle disagreements with other Christians?
